'''Karim Hiram López Mondaca''' (born 12 April 2007) is a Mexican professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).

==Early life==
López was born on 12 April 2007, in [[Hermosillo]], [[Sonora]], Mexico.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/264371/karim-lopez|website=Proballers.com|title=Karim Lopez}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/deportes/basquetbol/karim-lopez-la-joya-mexicana-que-apunta-a-jugar-en-la-nba|newspaper=[[Milenio]]|language=Spanish|title=Karim López, la joya mexicana que apunta a la NBA: "Es una meta a largo plazo"|trans-title=Karim López, the Mexican gem aiming for the NBA: "It's a long-term goal."|date=13 March 2025}}</ref> His father, [[Jesús Hiram López]], played for the [[Mexico national basketball team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ouresquina.com/2024/mexican-teen-prodigy-karim-lopez-nears-nba/|website=Our Esquina|title=Mexican teen prodigy Karim Lopez nears NBA|date=10 October 2024|author=de Jesus Ortiz, José}}</ref> After first trying out [[Association football|soccer]] and [[taekwondo]], he began playing [[basketball]] from a young age.<ref name="auto"/> He began training seriously for basketball at age 12 with the encouragement of his father, and was able to play against players up to five years older than him and still "held his own".<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/mexican-forward-karim-lopez-dreams-of-shooting-hoops-in-nba/|website=[[Andscape]]|title=Mexican forward Karim Lopez dreams of shooting hoops in NBA  |date=November 19, 2024|author=Spears, Marc J.}}</ref> At the age of 14, he received an offer to play professionally in Spain for the club [[Joventut Badalona]], and left his family to move there.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Professional career==
López played two seasons for Joventut Badalona's "B" team, from 2022 to 2024.<ref name="auto1"/> He was promoted to the senior squad in 2024 and appeared in four games during the 2023–24 season, scoring two points.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/> After the 2023–24 season, he left Joventut and signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) in August 2024 as a Next Star.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/basquetbol/nota/_/id/14406107/karim-lopez-mexicano-que-rompe-tendencia-en-la-nbl-de-australia|publisher=[[ESPN]]|language=Spanish|title=Karim López, el mexicano que rompe una tendencia en la NBL de Australia|trans-title=Karim López, the Mexican who breaks a trend in Australia's NBL|author=Uluc, Olgun|date=5 November 2024}}</ref> He impressed for the Breakers, becoming the youngest player in NBL history to record a [[double-double]] that October.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/es/noticias/quien-basquetbolista-mexicano-karim-lopez|website=[[Olympics.com]]|title=¿Quién es el basquetbolista mexicano Karim López, uno de los mejores prospectos para el Draft de la NBA 2026?|trans-title=Who is Mexican basketball player Karim López, one of the top prospects for the 2026 NBA Draft?|date=28 February 2025|author=Toledo, Jair}}</ref> Appearing in 25 games during the 2024–25 season, he averaged 9.6 points and 4.7 rebounds.<ref name="auto2"/>

On 30 January 2026, López scored a career-high 32 points in the Breakers' 97–95 win over [[Melbourne United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=A star is born: Lopez announces himself with 32 |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/karim-lopez-career-night-breakers-edge-melbourne-united |access-date=30 January 2026 |work=NBL.com.au |date=30 January 2026}}</ref> In the [[2025–26 NBL season]], the Breakers finished outside the finals spots in seventh at the end of the regular season but won the inaugural [[2025–26 NBL Ignite Cup|NBL Ignite Cup]] Final,<ref>{{cite news |title=MVP call backfires with NBL title contender stunned as non-finalist pulls upset in $400k final |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/mvp-call-backfires-with-nbl-title-contender-stunned-as-nonfinalist-pulls-upset-in-400k-final/news-story/87d6c19cb9ae35133a326f099e099f16 |access-date=22 February 2026 |work=Fox Sports |date=22 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> defeating the [[Adelaide 36ers]] 111–107 behind López's 12 points, eight rebounds, five assists and two steals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mennenga seals Breakers' dramatic Ignite triumph {{!}} Basketball.com.au |url=https://www.basketball.com.au/news/parker-jackson-cartwright-ignite-cup-dagger-breakers-36ers-feb-22-2026 |access-date=22 February 2026 |work=www.basketball.com.au |date=22 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=PJC leads Breakers to Ignite Cup crown |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/pjc-leads-breakers-to-ignite-cup-crown |access-date=22 February 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=22 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

On March 23, 2026, López declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Karim Lopez expected to be first Mexican-born basketball taken in first round of NBA Draft |url=https://nypost.com/2026/03/23/sports/mexican-born-karim-lopez-declares-for-2026-nba-draft/ |website=[[New York Post]] |date=March 23, 2026 |access-date=March 23, 2026}}</ref> where he is regarded as a top prospect.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/basquetbol/nota/_/id/14839152/karim-lopez-nba-seleccion-mexicana-ventaja-draft-2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|language=Spanish|title=La ventaja de Karim López para el Draft 2026 de la NBA|trans-title=Karim López's advantage for the 2026 NBA Draft|date=24 February 2025|author=Peña, Karen}}</ref>

==National team career==
López competed for Mexico at the 2022 Centrobasket U15 Championship.<ref name="auto"/> He then played at the [[2023 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]], notably scoring 23 points in a loss to the United States team.<ref name="auto1"/> He played for the senior national team in 2024 during the Olympic qualification tournament.<ref name="auto"/>
